lecons.titre: Greetings, Self-Introduction, and Nouns
savoirs_faire: Greet people at different periods of the day
Introduce self to others (Hello, my name is...)
Identify proper and common nouns in the home

exercices.enonce: Ayuk introduces himself in Douala: Hello, my name is Ayuk. Practice introducing your name.
exercices.astuce: Say 'Hello, my name is...' clearly.

quiz.question: How does Ayuk introduce himself to a classmate in Douala?
quiz.explication: 'Hello, my name is...' introduces your name.

quiz.question: Is 'Ayuk' a proper noun or a common noun?
quiz.explication: Names of specific people are proper nouns.

quiz.question: Which line type goes up and down sharply?
quiz.explication: A zigzag line goes back and forth sharply.

lecons.contenu:
Greetings, Self-Introduction, and Nouns

What you will learn:

  • Greet people at different periods of the day
  • Introduce self to others (Hello, my name is...)
  • Identify proper and common nouns in the home

In Douala (Week 1, Page 4), young Ayuk learns to greet others and introduce himself: 'Hello, my name is Ayuk.' We identify proper nouns like names and common nouns in the home.

lecons.titre: Introducing Others, Polite Requests, and Sitting Room Objects
savoirs_faire: Introduce others to peers (This is my sister...)
Make polite requests using 'sorry' and 'welcome'
Identify objects found in the sitting room

exercices.enonce: Ayuk introduces his sister in Douala: This is my sister. Identify a chair in sitting room.
exercices.astuce: Use polite words like 'welcome'.

quiz.question: Which polite word should Ayuk use to welcome guests in Douala?
quiz.explication: 'Welcome' is a polite greeting for guests.

quiz.question: How do you introduce your friend to others?
quiz.explication: 'This is my friend' introduces a peer.

quiz.question: Which object is found in the sitting room in Douala?
quiz.explication: A sofa or chair is sitting room furniture.

lecons.contenu:
Introducing Others, Polite Requests, and Sitting Room Objects

What you will learn:

  • Introduce others to peers (This is my sister...)
  • Make polite requests using 'sorry' and 'welcome'
  • Identify objects found in the sitting room

In Douala (Week 2, Page 5), Ayuk introduces his sister: 'This is my sister.' Polite words like 'sorry' and 'welcome' build good manners, and we name sitting room objects like chairs and sofas.

lecons.titre: Kitchen Vocabulary and Letter Sounds
savoirs_faire: Identify and name things found in the kitchen (pots, spoons)
Say letters and sounds of the alphabet
Write middle-case letters of the alphabet

exercices.enonce: Ayuk names kitchen items in Douala: Pot, spoon, plate. Read letter sounds.
exercices.astuce: Say the letter sound clearly.

quiz.question: Which item is used for cooking in the kitchen in Douala?
quiz.explication: Pots are used for cooking food.

quiz.question: Which letter sound does 'Pot' start with?
quiz.explication: 'Pot' begins with the sound P.

quiz.question: What pronoun replaces Ayuk when speaking about himself?
quiz.explication: The personal pronoun 'I' refers to oneself.

lecons.contenu:
Kitchen Vocabulary and Letter Sounds

What you will learn:

  • Identify and name things found in the kitchen (pots, spoons)
  • Say letters and sounds of the alphabet
  • Write middle-case letters of the alphabet

In Douala (Week 3, Page 5-6), Ayuk learns kitchen vocabulary (pots, plates, spoons) and practices saying letter sounds and writing middle-case letters.

lecons.titre: Domestic Animals, Animal Sounds, and Present Continuous Tense
savoirs_faire: Produce sounds made by domestic animals (dog barks, cat meows)
Read names of domestic animals and spell three-letter words (dog, cat)
Use verbs in the present continuous tense (-ing forms)

exercices.enonce: Ayuk imitates animal sounds in Douala: The dog barks woof, the cat meows meow. Spell C-A-T.
exercices.astuce: Imitate domestic animal sounds clearly.

quiz.question: What sound does a dog make in Douala?
quiz.explication: A dog barks 'woof woof'.

quiz.question: Spell the three-letter word for a domestic pet animal: C-A-T. What is it?
quiz.explication: C-A-T spells Cat.

quiz.question: Which verb is in the present continuous tense (-ing form)?
quiz.explication: 'Running' ends in -ing for present continuous tense.

lecons.contenu:
Domestic Animals, Animal Sounds, and Present Continuous Tense

What you will learn:

  • Produce sounds made by domestic animals (dog barks, cat meows)
  • Read names of domestic animals and spell three-letter words (dog, cat)
  • Use verbs in the present continuous tense (-ing forms)

In Douala (Week 4, Page 6), Ayuk learns domestic animals (dog, cat, goat, sheep) and their sounds! We spell 3-letter words like C-A-T and D-O-G, and practice verbs in the present continuous tense ('The dog is running').

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 1 to 10 and Introduction of Sets
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 1 to 10
Define a mathematical set of objects
Name and identify days of the week

exercices.enonce: Ekema counts 5 oranges in Bamenda. Write 5 in words.
exercices.astuce: 5 = Five.

quiz.question: How is the number 5 written in words in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 5 is written as Five.

quiz.question: What is a collection of items called in mathematics?
quiz.explication: A set is a collection of items.

quiz.question: What day comes after Monday?
quiz.explication: Tuesday follows Monday.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 1 to 10 and Introduction of Sets

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 1 to 10
  • Define a mathematical set of objects
  • Name and identify days of the week

In Bamenda (Week 1, Page 38), Ekema counts items at home from 1 to 10. A set is a collection of items. We also learn the days of the week starting with Monday!

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 11 to 20 and Plane Shapes
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 11 to 20
Form sets using real objects at home
Identify plane shapes (circle, square, rectangle)

exercices.enonce: Ekema counts 15 sticks in Bamenda. Identify a round circle shape.
exercices.astuce: A circle is round like a coin.

quiz.question: What number comes right after 14 in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 15 comes right after 14.

quiz.question: Which plane shape is completely round like a coin?
quiz.explication: A circle is round with no straight sides.

quiz.question: How many straight sides does a square have?
quiz.explication: A square has 4 equal straight sides.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 11 to 20 and Plane Shapes

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 11 to 20
  • Form sets using real objects at home
  • Identify plane shapes (circle, square, rectangle)

In Bamenda (Week 2, Page 38-39), Ekema counts from 11 to 20. We form sets of objects and recognize basic plane shapes around the home like circles, squares, and rectangles.

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 21 to 30 and Set Symbols
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 21 to 30
Identify mathematical set symbols
Identify and name activities of the week

exercices.enonce: Ekema counts 25 stones in Bamenda. Write 25 in words.
exercices.astuce: 25 = Twenty-five.

quiz.question: What number comes right after 24 in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 25 comes right after 24.

quiz.question: How is 20 written in words?
quiz.explication: 20 is written as Twenty.

quiz.question: What symbol represents a mathematical set?
quiz.explication: Curly brackets { } enclose set elements.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 21 to 30 and Set Symbols

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 21 to 30
  • Identify mathematical set symbols
  • Identify and name activities of the week

In Bamenda (Week 3, Page 39), Ekema counts from 21 to 30. We study set symbols and connect numbers to daily activities of the week!

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 31 to 40 and Shape Attributes
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 31 to 40
Identify sides and corners of geometric shapes
Revise monthly mathematics concepts

exercices.enonce: Ekema counts 35 mangoes in Bamenda. Count up to 40.

quiz.question: What number comes right after 39 in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 40 comes right after 39.

quiz.question: How many corners does a square shape have?
quiz.explication: A square has 4 corners and 4 sides.

quiz.question: What number is written as 'Thirty-one' in figures?
quiz.explication: Thirty-one is written as 31.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 31 to 40 and Shape Attributes

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 31 to 40
  • Identify sides and corners of geometric shapes
  • Revise monthly mathematics concepts

In Bamenda (Week 4, Page 40), Ekema completes the monthly counting progression from 31 to 40. We count sides and corners of plane shapes and review September mathematics!

lecons.titre: Human Body Parts and Local Machines
savoirs_faire: Identify and differentiate main parts of the human body
Identify types of simple machines in the locality
Describe features of the immediate home environment

exercices.enonce: Ayuk points to his head and legs in Buea. Name a simple machine at home.
exercices.astuce: Head, hands, legs are body parts.

quiz.question: Which body part contains the eyes, ears, and mouth in Buea?
quiz.explication: The head contains eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.

quiz.question: Which tool is a simple machine used to cut paper or cloth at home?
quiz.explication: Scissors are simple cutting machines.

quiz.question: What body parts do we use for walking in Buea?
quiz.explication: Legs and feet are used for walking.

lecons.contenu:
Human Body Parts and Local Machines

What you will learn:

  • Identify and differentiate main parts of the human body
  • Identify types of simple machines in the locality
  • Describe features of the immediate home environment

In Buea (Week 1, Page 62 & 77), Ayuk identifies main body parts (head, trunk, limbs) and simple machines found around the home like scissors and hand tools.

lecons.titre: Functions of Body Parts and Kitchen Machines
savoirs_faire: Associate body parts to their specific functions
Identify machines found in the kitchen (grater, mortar)
Explain safety rules around kitchen machines

exercices.enonce: Ayuk uses his eyes to see and grater in kitchen in Buea. What do eyes do?
exercices.astuce: Eyes see; ears hear; nose smells.

quiz.question: Which sense organ is used to hear sounds in Buea?
quiz.explication: Ears are used for hearing sounds.

quiz.question: Which kitchen tool is used to crush spices or food in Buea?
quiz.explication: Mortar and pestles crush spices and cassava.

quiz.question: Why must sharp kitchen tools be handled with care?
quiz.explication: Careful handling prevents cuts.

lecons.contenu:
Functions of Body Parts and Kitchen Machines

What you will learn:

  • Associate body parts to their specific functions
  • Identify machines found in the kitchen (grater, mortar)
  • Explain safety rules around kitchen machines

In Buea (Week 2, Page 62 & 77), Ayuk learns body part functions: eyes see, ears hear, legs walk. We identify kitchen tools like graters and mortars, and practice safety rules.

lecons.titre: Personal Hygiene and Uses of Machines
savoirs_faire: Demonstrate daily care of the body using soap, sponge, and towel
State uses of simple machines at home
Explain daily habits for bodily cleanliness

exercices.enonce: Ayuk washes his body with sponge and towel in Buea. Name two bath items.
exercices.astuce: Soap, water, sponge, towel.

quiz.question: What item is used to wash away dirt from the skin during a bath?
quiz.explication: Soap and water wash away dirt.

quiz.question: What do we use to dry our body after bathing in Buea?
quiz.explication: A clean towel dries the body.

quiz.question: Why do we use simple machines like knives or scissors at home?
options: To make work easier and faster
quiz.explication: Machines make work easier.

lecons.contenu:
Personal Hygiene and Uses of Machines

What you will learn:

  • Demonstrate daily care of the body using soap, sponge, and towel
  • State uses of simple machines at home
  • Explain daily habits for bodily cleanliness

In Buea (Week 3, Page 62 & 77), Ayuk practices personal hygiene. Bathing daily with soap, water, sponge, and towel keeps the body clean. We also explore how machines make home tasks easier.

lecons.titre: Cleaning Items and Care of Machines
savoirs_faire: Identify things used in cleaning the body
Describe how to clean and care for machines at home
State safety rules for storing sharp tools

exercices.enonce: Ayuk cleans and stores home tools in Buea. How to store scissors?
exercices.astuce: Clean tools and store in a safe box.

quiz.question: Which of these is used to keep teeth clean and healthy?
quiz.explication: A toothbrush and toothpaste clean teeth.

quiz.question: How do we care for home tools after use?
options: Clean them and store in a safe place
quiz.explication: Cleaning and safe storage preserve tools.

quiz.question: Why should tools be kept away from small children?
quiz.explication: Safe storage prevents accidents.

lecons.contenu:
Cleaning Items and Care of Machines

What you will learn:

  • Identify things used in cleaning the body
  • Describe how to clean and care for machines at home
  • State safety rules for storing sharp tools

In Buea (Week 4, Page 62 & 77), Ayuk identifies body cleaning items (toothbrush, toothpaste, soap) and learns how to clean, dry, and store home machines safely!

lecons.titre: Sons du français et supports écrits
savoirs_faire: Écouter et reproduire les bruits et onomatopées
Découvrir divers supports écrits (livres, étiquettes)
Écrire des lettres et des graphies de phonèmes

exercices.enonce: Écoute les bruits avec Ngono à Yaoundé et nomme les images d'un livre.
exercices.astuce: Imite le bruit des animaux et des objets.

quiz.question: Quel support écrit contient des histoires et des images à Yaoundé ?
quiz.explication: Le livre contient des images et des histoires.

quiz.question: Comment fait le chat en onomatopée ?
quiz.explication: Le chat fait miaou.

quiz.question: Que regarde Ngono dans sa classe à Yaoundé ?
quiz.explication: Les étiquettes aident à reconnaître les mots.

lecons.contenu:
Sons du français et supports écrits

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Écouter et reproduire les bruits et onomatopées
  • Découvrir divers supports écrits (livres, étiquettes)
  • Écrire des lettres et des graphies de phonèmes

À Yaoundé (Semaine 1, Page 82), Ngono écoute les sons du français, imite les bruits et découvre les livres et étiquettes pour apprendre à lire.

lecons.titre: Graphies des phonèmes et écriture des mots
savoirs_faire: Écrire des mots simples avec les phonèmes étudiés
Reconnaître des noms communs du foyer
Feuilleter des albums et étiquettes

exercices.enonce: Écris des mots simples avec Ngono à Yaoundé : papa, maman.
exercices.astuce: Associe les sons des lettres.

quiz.question: Quel mot désigne le père de famille en français à Yaoundé ?
quiz.explication: Papa désigne le père.

quiz.question: Quel mot désigne la mère de famille ?
quiz.explication: Maman désigne la mère.

quiz.question: Comment s'appelle l'ensemble des lettres qu'on écrit ?
quiz.explication: L'alphabet regroupe les lettres de la langue.

lecons.contenu:
Graphies des phonèmes et écriture des mots

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Écrire des mots simples avec les phonèmes étudiés
  • Reconnaître des noms communs du foyer
  • Feuilleter des albums et étiquettes

À Yaoundé (Semaine 2, Page 82), Ngono écrit ses premiers mots simples comme 'papa' et 'maman' en associant les sons des graphies écrites.

lecons.titre: Salutations et vocabulaire de la maison
savoirs_faire: Saluer et prendre congé (Bonjour, bonsoir, au revoir, merci)
Utiliser le vocabulaire usuel de la maison
Écrire des lettres de l'alphabet

exercices.enonce: Salue la famille avec Ngono à Yaoundé : Bonjour papa, bonsoir maman !
exercices.astuce: Bonjour le matin, bonsoir le soir.

quiz.question: Comment salue-t-on le matin à Yaoundé ?
quiz.explication: Le matin, on dit Bonjour.

quiz.question: Que dit-on quand on s'en va ?
quiz.explication: On dit Au revoir en partant.

quiz.question: Que dit-on quand on reçoit un cadeau ?
quiz.explication: On dit Merci pour exprimer sa gratitude.

lecons.contenu:
Salutations et vocabulaire de la maison

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Saluer et prendre congé (Bonjour, bonsoir, au revoir, merci)
  • Utiliser le vocabulaire usuel de la maison
  • Écrire des lettres de l'alphabet

À Yaoundé (Semaine 3, Page 82), Ngono apprend les formules de politesse : Bonjour, Bonsoir, Au revoir, Merci, et découvre les mots usuels du foyer.

lecons.titre: Home Rules and Regulations
savoirs_faire: State home rules and regulations
Demonstrate obedience to parents at home
Keep the home environment tidy

exercices.enonce: Amina lists rules at home in Garoua: Respect elders, clean your room.
exercices.astuce: Home rules keep the house safe and orderly.

quiz.question: What is a good rule to follow at home in Garoua?
quiz.explication: Respecting parents and helping at home creates harmony.

quiz.question: Why do parents establish home rules in Garoua?
options: To keep children safe and disciplined
quiz.explication: Rules protect children and ensure order.

quiz.question: How can children help keep the home clean?
options: Putting toys and books in their proper place
quiz.explication: Tidying toys keeps the home neat.

lecons.contenu:
Home Rules and Regulations

What you will learn:

  • State home rules and regulations
  • Demonstrate obedience to parents at home
  • Keep the home environment tidy

In Garoua (Week 1, Page 91), Amina learns home rules. Respecting elders, obeying parents, and keeping toys organized promote safety and peace at home.

lecons.titre: School Rules and Regulations
savoirs_faire: List school rules and regulations
Explain the importance of punctuality
Show respect to teachers and classmates

exercices.enonce: Amina lists school rules in Garoua: Arrive on time, raise hand before speaking.
exercices.astuce: Punctuality means arriving on time.

quiz.question: What does punctuality at school mean in Garoua?
options: Arriving at school on time every day
quiz.explication: Punctuality means being on time.

quiz.question: How do pupils show respect to teachers in class?
options: Listening attentively and raising hands to speak
quiz.explication: Listening and raising hands show respect.

quiz.question: Why are school rules important?
options: They help everyone learn in safety and order
quiz.explication: School rules maintain order and safe learning.

lecons.contenu:
School Rules and Regulations

What you will learn:

  • List school rules and regulations
  • Explain the importance of punctuality
  • Show respect to teachers and classmates

In Garoua (Week 2, Page 91), Amina learns school rules. Arriving on time, listening to teachers, and respecting classmates build a peaceful school environment.

lecons.titre: Community Rules and Peaceful Living
savoirs_faire: State community rules and regulations
Explain importance of living peacefully with neighbors
Greet neighbors respectfully in the locality

exercices.enonce: Amina greets neighbors respectfully in Garoua. Why live peacefully?
exercices.astuce: Peaceful living helps everyone feel safe.

quiz.question: How should we treat neighbors in our community in Garoua?
options: Greet them politely and live in peace
quiz.explication: Greeting neighbors politely fosters peace.

quiz.question: Why must public property in the neighborhood be protected?
quiz.explication: Public property serves all community members.

quiz.question: What value promotes harmony among community members?
quiz.explication: Respect and peace bring community harmony.

lecons.contenu:
Community Rules and Peaceful Living

What you will learn:

  • State community rules and regulations
  • Explain importance of living peacefully with neighbors
  • Greet neighbors respectfully in the locality

In Garoua (Week 3, Page 91), Amina discovers community rules. Living peacefully with neighbors, respecting shared spaces, and greeting elders build strong neighborhoods.

lecons.titre: Outline Rules and Peaceful Co-existence
savoirs_faire: Outline home and community rules
Demonstrate peaceful co-existence with peers
Revise monthly citizenship rules

exercices.enonce: Amina outlines rules for peaceful living in Garoua. Practice sharing toys.
exercices.astuce: Sharing toys builds friendship and peace.

quiz.question: What happens when everyone follows home and community rules in Garoua?
options: There is safety, peace, and harmony
quiz.explication: Following rules creates safety and harmony.

quiz.question: How do children demonstrate peaceful co-existence at play?
quiz.explication: Sharing toys fosters peaceful play.

quiz.question: Who should we report dangerous situations to in the community?
quiz.explication: Always report dangers to trusted adults.

lecons.contenu:
Outline Rules and Peaceful Co-existence

What you will learn:

  • Outline home and community rules
  • Demonstrate peaceful co-existence with peers
  • Revise monthly citizenship rules

In Garoua (Week 4, Page 91), Amina outlines home and community rules, learning that fair play, sharing, and obedience ensure peaceful co-existence for everyone!

lecons.titre: Traditional ICT Tools
savoirs_faire: Identify and draw traditional ICT tools (talking drum, gong, horn)
Describe shapes of traditional ICT tools
Show care for drawing materials

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla draws a talking drum in Douala. Name one traditional ICT tool.
exercices.astuce: Talking drums and gongs sent messages in villages.

quiz.question: Which traditional instrument sent messages across villages in early Cameroon?
quiz.explication: Talking drums transmitted messages across distances.

quiz.question: How did villagers know a chief's meeting was called in early times?
options: By hearing the village gong or drum
quiz.explication: Gongs and drums signaled community meetings.

quiz.question: What drawing material do we use to sketch a drum in Douala?
quiz.explication: Pencil and paper are drawing tools.

lecons.contenu:
Traditional ICT Tools

What you will learn:

  • Identify and draw traditional ICT tools (talking drum, gong, horn)
  • Describe shapes of traditional ICT tools
  • Show care for drawing materials

In Douala (Week 1, Page 146), Ekwalla identifies traditional communication tools. Before phones, talking drums and gongs alerted villages and shared important news!

lecons.titre: Uses of Traditional ICT Tools
savoirs_faire: State the correct uses of traditional ICT tools in the village
Explain how drum beats communicate different messages
Respect traditional cultural instruments

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla explains how gongs call community gatherings in Douala.
exercices.astuce: Gongs call people together for meetings.

quiz.question: What signal did a wooden drum beat send in traditional villages?
options: An announcement or call to gathering
quiz.explication: Drum beats signaled announcements or gatherings.

quiz.question: Which tool was blown to sound an emergency alert in early times?
quiz.explication: Horns were blown to alert villagers.

quiz.question: Why are traditional ICT tools still respected in Cameroon?
options: They represent rich cultural heritage and history
quiz.explication: Traditional tools preserve cultural heritage.

lecons.contenu:
Uses of Traditional ICT Tools

What you will learn:

  • State the correct uses of traditional ICT tools in the village
  • Explain how drum beats communicate different messages
  • Respect traditional cultural instruments

In Douala (Week 2, Page 147), Ekwalla learns the specific uses of traditional ICT tools: gongs to call meetings and horns for emergency alerts across the village.

lecons.titre: Modern ICT Tools
savoirs_faire: Identify and draw modern ICT tools (radio, television, telephone)
Distinguish traditional tools from modern tools
Handle drawing materials neatly

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla draws a radio and telephone in Douala. Name two modern tools.
exercices.astuce: Radio, TV, and telephone are modern tools.

quiz.question: Which modern ICT tool at home broadcasts audio news in Douala?
quiz.explication: Radios broadcast audio news and music.

quiz.question: Which modern ICT tool displays moving pictures and video?
quiz.explication: Televisions display video and moving images.

quiz.question: Which device is used to speak to a person in another town?
quiz.explication: Telephones connect voice calls across towns.

lecons.contenu:
Modern ICT Tools

What you will learn:

  • Identify and draw modern ICT tools (radio, television, telephone)
  • Distinguish traditional tools from modern tools
  • Handle drawing materials neatly

In Douala (Week 3, Page 147), Ekwalla identifies and draws modern ICT tools found at home: radios, televisions, and telephones that transmit information instantly!

lecons.titre: Uses of Modern ICT Tools and Electrical Safety
savoirs_faire: State the correct uses of modern ICT tools (telephone, TV, radio)
Describe how news and lessons are broadcast on radio/TV
Observe safety around electrical plugs and cables at home

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla listens to educational programs on TV in Douala with parents. Why use TV?
exercices.astuce: TV provides news and educational programs.

quiz.question: Why do families watch television at home in Douala?
options: For news, weather, and educational programs
quiz.explication: TV provides news and educational content.

quiz.question: Why must electrical plugs of TV and radio never be touched with wet hands?
options: To prevent electric shocks and danger
quiz.explication: Wet hands conduct electricity and cause shocks.

quiz.question: How do telephones help families stay connected in Cameroon?
options: By making instant voice calls to relatives
quiz.explication: Telephones enable instant voice communication.

lecons.contenu:
Uses of Modern ICT Tools and Electrical Safety

What you will learn:

  • State the correct uses of modern ICT tools (telephone, TV, radio)
  • Describe how news and lessons are broadcast on radio/TV
  • Observe safety around electrical plugs and cables at home

In Douala (Week 4, Page 147), Ekwalla learns the uses of modern ICT tools for educational programs and news, while emphasizing safety rules around electrical plugs and wires!

lecons.titre: Things in Town, Town Stories, and Articles a/an
savoirs_faire: Name things found in town (market, cars, stores)
Tell simple stories about life in town
Use articles 'a' and 'an' correctly before nouns

exercices.enonce: Ayuk names items in Douala town: A car, an apple, a market. Use 'a' or 'an'.
exercices.astuce: Use 'an' before vowel sounds (a, e, i, o, u).

quiz.question: Which article comes before 'apple' in Douala town?
quiz.explication: 'An' is used before vowel sounds like 'apple'.

quiz.question: Which social amenity in town is used for buying food?
quiz.explication: Markets are town amenities for buying food.

quiz.question: Which article comes before 'car'?
quiz.explication: 'A' is used before consonant sounds like 'car'.

lecons.contenu:
Things in Town, Town Stories, and Articles a/an

What you will learn:

  • Name things found in town (market, cars, stores)
  • Tell simple stories about life in town
  • Use articles 'a' and 'an' correctly before nouns

In Douala town (Week 1, Page 7), Ayuk explores busy streets, markets, and vehicles. We practice telling stories about town life and using articles 'a car' and 'an apple'.

lecons.titre: Town Personalities, Short Reading, and Nouns
savoirs_faire: Name and describe personalities in town (Mayor, doctor)
Read short sentences and answer comprehension questions
Identify countable and uncountable nouns

exercices.enonce: Ayuk meets the Mayor in Douala town. Is 'water' countable or uncountable?
exercices.astuce: Water is uncountable; apples are countable.

quiz.question: Who leads a municipal council in a town like Douala?
quiz.explication: The Mayor is a town authority personality.

quiz.question: Which noun can be counted individually?
quiz.explication: Apples can be counted as 1, 2, 3 apples.

quiz.question: Read: 'The doctor helps sick people in town.' Who helps sick people?
quiz.explication: Doctors care for sick people in health centers.

lecons.contenu:
Town Personalities, Short Reading, and Nouns

What you will learn:

  • Name and describe personalities in town (Mayor, doctor)
  • Read short sentences and answer comprehension questions
  • Identify countable and uncountable nouns

In Douala (Week 2, Page 7-8), Ayuk meets town personalities like doctors and mayors. We read short sentences and distinguish countable nouns (books, apples) from uncountable nouns (water, milk).

lecons.titre: Village Places, Personalities, and Plural Nouns
savoirs_faire: Name things, important places, and personalities in the village
Write short sentences with subject, verb, and object
Form plural of nouns by adding -s

exercices.enonce: Ayuk visits his village in Buea and meets the Chief. Write plural of 'house'.

quiz.explication: The Chief is the traditional leader of a village.

quiz.question: What is the plural form of 'car'?
quiz.explication: Plural of car is cars.

quiz.question: In the sentence 'Ayuk sees a house', what is the subject?
quiz.explication: Ayuk is the subject performing the action.

lecons.contenu:
Village Places, Personalities, and Plural Nouns

What you will learn:

  • Name things, important places, and personalities in the village
  • Write short sentences with subject, verb, and object
  • Form plural of nouns by adding -s

In Buea village (Week 3, Page 8), Ayuk visits the palace and meets the Chief. We learn village landmarks and practice forming plural nouns like house -> houses and car -> cars.

lecons.titre: Village Activities, Regular Past Tense, and Stories
savoirs_faire: Tell stories about village life and name village activities (farming, hunting, fishing)
Write regular verbs in the past tense (-ed forms)
Spell words using common phonetic patterns

exercices.enonce: Ayuk listens to village stories in Buea: Farming, hunting, fishing. Write past tense of 'walk'.
exercices.astuce: Walk -> Walked.

quiz.question: Which activity is commonly done by villagers in Buea?
quiz.explication: Farming and fishing are traditional village activities.

quiz.question: What is the regular past tense of the verb 'walk'?
quiz.explication: Regular past tense adds -ed: walked.

quiz.question: What is the past tense of 'farm'?
quiz.explication: Farmed is the past tense of farm.

lecons.contenu:
Village Activities, Regular Past Tense, and Stories

What you will learn:

  • Tell stories about village life and name village activities (farming, hunting, fishing)
  • Write regular verbs in the past tense (-ed forms)
  • Spell words using common phonetic patterns

In Buea village (Week 4, Page 8-9), Ayuk hears elders tell stories of farming, hunting, palm tapping, and fishing. We write regular past tense verbs like walked, farmed, and played!

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 41 to 50 and Months of the Year
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 41 to 50
Identify set symbols in mathematics
Name, identify, and write months of the year

exercices.astuce: 45 = Forty-five.

quiz.question: What number comes right after 49 in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 50 follows 49.

quiz.explication: 40 is written as Forty.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 41 to 50 and Months of the Year

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 41 to 50
  • Identify set symbols in mathematics
  • Name, identify, and write months of the year

In Bamenda (Week 1, Page 41), Ekema counts from 41 to 50. We study mathematical set symbols and memorize calendar months starting with January!

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 51 to 60 and Carving Shapes
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 51 to 60
Identify and write set symbols
Carve and trace plane shapes using craft materials

exercices.enonce: Ekema counts 55 cassava roots in Bamenda. Carve a square shape out of paper.
exercices.astuce: 55 = Fifty-five.

quiz.question: What number comes right after 59 in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 60 follows 59.

quiz.question: How is 50 written in words?
quiz.explication: 50 is written as Fifty.

quiz.question: Which plane shape has 4 equal straight sides?
quiz.explication: A square has 4 equal straight sides.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 51 to 60 and Carving Shapes

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 51 to 60
  • Identify and write set symbols
  • Carve and trace plane shapes using craft materials

In Bamenda (Week 2, Page 41-42), Ekema counts from 51 to 60. We practice writing set symbols and carving plane geometric shapes like squares and circles!

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 61 to 70 and Important Dates
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 61 to 70
Identify and name mathematical sets
Name important dates of the year on the calendar

exercices.enonce: Ekema counts 65 plantains in Bamenda. Write 65 in figures.
exercices.astuce: 65 = 6 tens and 5 units.

quiz.question: What number comes right after 69 in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 70 follows 69.

quiz.question: How is 60 written in words?
quiz.explication: 60 is written as Sixty.

quiz.question: What tool do we use to locate important national dates?
quiz.explication: A calendar marks important dates.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 61 to 70 and Important Dates

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 61 to 70
  • Identify and name mathematical sets
  • Name important dates of the year on the calendar

In Bamenda (Week 3, Page 42), Ekema extends her counting from 61 to 70. We learn to name set contents and identify important national holiday dates on a calendar!

lecons.titre: Counting Numbers 71 to 80 and Triangle Construction
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers in figures and words from 71 to 80
Name and form sets of real objects
Construct a triangle shape with 3 straight sides

exercices.enonce: Ekema counts up to 80 in Bamenda. Construct a triangle with 3 sticks.
exercices.astuce: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

quiz.question: What number comes right after 79 in Bamenda?
quiz.explication: 80 follows 79.

quiz.question: How many straight sides does a constructed triangle have?
quiz.explication: A triangle has 3 straight sides.

quiz.question: How is 70 written in words?
quiz.explication: 70 is written as Seventy.

lecons.contenu:
Counting Numbers 71 to 80 and Triangle Construction

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers in figures and words from 71 to 80
  • Name and form sets of real objects
  • Construct a triangle shape with 3 straight sides

In Bamenda (Week 4, Page 42-43), Ekema completes the monthly counting progression from 71 to 80! We practice forming sets and constructing triangles using sticks and craft paper.

lecons.titre: School Environment and Environmental Materials
savoirs_faire: Identify components of the school environment
Identify common types of materials in the locality (wood, stone, paper)
Observe cleanliness around school grounds

exercices.enonce: Ayuk explores school grounds in Buea. Name a common material around school.
exercices.astuce: Wood, stone, paper, and soil.

quiz.question: Which of these is a component of the school environment in Buea?
quiz.explication: Classrooms and playgrounds form school grounds.

quiz.question: Which natural material comes from trees and is used for desks?
quiz.explication: Wood comes from trees.

quiz.question: Why should school grounds be kept clean in Buea?
options: To maintain a healthy learning environment
quiz.explication: Clean grounds promote health.

lecons.contenu:
School Environment and Environmental Materials

What you will learn:

  • Identify components of the school environment
  • Identify common types of materials in the locality (wood, stone, paper)
  • Observe cleanliness around school grounds

In Buea (Week 1, Page 69 & 78), Ayuk identifies school environment parts (classrooms, yard) and common materials like wood, stone, and paper used to make furniture and tools.

lecons.titre: School Family and Dangerous Materials
savoirs_faire: Identify members of the school family (teachers, pupils, parents)
Identify dangerous materials in the school environment (broken glass, rusty nails)
Demonstrate care for the school environment

exercices.enonce: Ayuk identifies members of school family in Buea. Name one dangerous object to avoid.
exercices.astuce: Broken glass, sharp nails, razor blades.

quiz.question: Who belongs to the school family in Buea?
quiz.explication: Teachers, pupils, and parents form the school community.

quiz.question: Which material is dangerous if found on the playground?
quiz.explication: Broken glass and nails cause injuries.

quiz.question: What should a pupil do if they see broken glass in the school yard?
options: Pick it up with bare hands
quiz.explication: Always alert a teacher about sharp hazards.

lecons.contenu:
School Family and Dangerous Materials

What you will learn:

  • Identify members of the school family (teachers, pupils, parents)
  • Identify dangerous materials in the school environment (broken glass, rusty nails)
  • Demonstrate care for the school environment

In Buea (Week 2, Page 69 & 78), Ayuk learns about the school family (teachers, pupils, parents). We identify dangerous hazards like broken glass and rusty nails to keep everyone safe!

lecons.titre: Types of Flowers and Avoiding School Hazards
savoirs_faire: Identify different types of flowers in the garden
State ways to avoid dangerous materials in the school environment
Participate in keeping flower beds clean

exercices.enonce: Ayuk waters flowers in school garden in Buea. How to avoid hazards?
exercices.astuce: Wear shoes and do not touch sharp objects.

quiz.question: Why do schools plant flowers in Buea?
quiz.explication: Flowers beautify and freshen the school.

quiz.question: How can pupils avoid injuries from sharp objects at school?
options: Wearing footwear and avoiding sharp trash
quiz.explication: Wearing shoes protects feet from sharp items.

quiz.question: What tool is used for gardening and weeding flower beds?
quiz.explication: Hoes are used for weeding garden beds.

lecons.contenu:
Types of Flowers and Avoiding School Hazards

What you will learn:

  • Identify different types of flowers in the garden
  • State ways to avoid dangerous materials in the school environment
  • Participate in keeping flower beds clean

In Buea (Week 3, Page 69 & 78), Ayuk studies garden flowers that beautify school grounds. We practice safety rules to avoid hazardous materials on campus.

lecons.titre: Types of Plants and Material Recycling
savoirs_faire: Identify different types of plants in the locality
Show interest in recycling and re-using common materials
Describe proper handling of paper and plastic

exercices.enonce: Ayuk identifies plants and recycles paper boxes in Buea. What is recycling?
exercices.astuce: Recycling turns old materials into useful new items.

quiz.question: Which of these is a plant found around the school in Buea?
quiz.explication: Grasses and trees are living plants.

quiz.question: What is recycling of materials?
options: Re-using old materials to make useful items
quiz.explication: Recycling transforms old materials into new items.

quiz.question: Which material can be collected and recycled into new paper?
quiz.explication: Waste paper is recycled into new paper products.

lecons.contenu:
Types of Plants and Material Recycling

What you will learn:

  • Identify different types of plants in the locality
  • Show interest in recycling and re-using common materials
  • Describe proper handling of paper and plastic

In Buea (Week 4, Page 69 & 78), Ayuk discovers plant diversity (shrubs, trees, grasses) and learns the value of recycling waste paper and plastics to protect our environment!

lecons.titre: Formules d'introduction et voyelles Aa-Ee
savoirs_faire: Utiliser les formules de présentation (Voici, voilà, s'appeler)
Reconnaître et lire les voyelles (Aa, Oo, Ii, Uu, Ee)
Distinguer les homophones a / as / à

exercices.enonce: Ngono présente un camarade à Yaoundé : Voici Paul, il s'appelle Paul. Lis les voyelles.
exercices.astuce: Voici montre quelqu'un qui est proche.

quiz.question: Quelle formule utilise Ngono pour présenter son ami proche à Yaoundé ?
quiz.explication: 'Voici' présente une personne ou un objet proche.

quiz.question: Parmi ces lettres, laquelle est une voyelle ?
quiz.explication: Aa est une voyelle.

quiz.question: Complète : Il ___ un livre (verbe avoir).
quiz.explication: 'a' sans accent est le verbe avoir (3e personne).

lecons.contenu:
Formules d'introduction et voyelles Aa-Ee

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Utiliser les formules de présentation (Voici, voilà, s'appeler)
  • Reconnaître et lire les voyelles (Aa, Oo, Ii, Uu, Ee)
  • Distinguer les homophones a / as / à

À Yaoundé (Semaine 1, Page 83), Ngono apprend à présenter ses amis ('Voici Paul', 'Il s'appelle Paul'). Nous étudions les voyelles (Aa, Oo, Ii, Uu, Ee) et les homophones a/as/à.

lecons.titre: Pronoms personnels et écriture des voyelles
savoirs_faire: Utiliser les pronoms personnels sujets (Je, tu, il, elle)
Écrire des mots simples avec les voyelles étudiées
Distinguer le genre et le nombre des noms

exercices.enonce: Ngono parle à Yaoundé : Je suis un élève, tu es mon ami, il joue. Complète avec 'elle'.
exercices.astuce: Elle désigne une fille ou une femme.

quiz.question: Quel pronom personnel remplace une fille à Yaoundé ?
quiz.explication: 'Elle' désigne le genre féminin.

quiz.question: Quel pronom personnel utilise Ngono pour parler de lui-même ?
quiz.explication: 'Je' désigne la personne qui parle.

quiz.question: Complète : Tu ___ un sac (verbe avoir).
quiz.explication: 'as' s'écrit avec la 2e personne (Tu as).

lecons.contenu:
Pronoms personnels et écriture des voyelles

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Utiliser les pronoms personnels sujets (Je, tu, il, elle)
  • Écrire des mots simples avec les voyelles étudiées
  • Distinguer le genre et le nombre des noms

À Yaoundé (Semaine 2, Page 83), Ngono s'entraîne à utiliser les pronoms personnels (Je, tu, il, elle) pour parler de soi et des camarades, tout en écrivant des mots composés des voyelles étudiées.

lecons.titre: Questions simples et vocabulaire du village
savoirs_faire: Poser des questions simples (Est-ce que...?)
Utiliser le vocabulaire usuel relatif à la ville et au village
Écrire des mots simples avec les voyelles

exercices.enonce: Ngono pose une question à Yaoundé : Est-ce que tu viens au marché ? Pose une question.
exercices.astuce: Utilise 'Est-ce que' au début de la question.

quiz.question: Quelle formule utilise Ngono pour poser une question à Yaoundé ?
quiz.explication: 'Est-ce que' introduit une phrase interrogative.

quiz.question: Quel mot appartient au vocabulaire du village ou de la ville ?
quiz.explication: Le marché et la chefferie sont des lieux d'un village/ville.

quiz.question: Complète : Il va ___ la maison (préposition).
quiz.explication: 'à' avec accent est la préposition de lieu.

lecons.contenu:
Questions simples et vocabulaire du village

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Poser des questions simples (Est-ce que...?)
  • Utiliser le vocabulaire usuel relatif à la ville et au village
  • Écrire des mots simples avec les voyelles

À Yaoundé (Semaine 3, Page 83), Ngono apprend à poser des questions avec 'Est-ce que...?' et utilise le vocabulaire de la ville et du village pour s'exprimer clairement.

lecons.titre: Personalities: School Authorities
savoirs_faire: State school authorities (Headteacher, teachers, school staff)
Explain the roles of school authorities
Demonstrate respect toward school leaders

exercices.enonce: Amina identifies school authorities in Garoua: Headteacher and class teacher. Who leads the school?
exercices.astuce: The Headteacher heads the primary school.

quiz.question: Who is the head authority of a primary school in Garoua?
quiz.explication: The Headteacher manages the school.

quiz.question: What is the role of a class teacher at school?
options: To teach lessons and guide pupils
quiz.explication: Teachers educate and guide pupils.

quiz.question: How do pupils show respect to the Headteacher?
options: Greeting politely and obeying school rules
quiz.explication: Polite greetings and obedience show respect.

lecons.contenu:
Personalities: School Authorities

What you will learn:

  • State school authorities (Headteacher, teachers, school staff)
  • Explain the roles of school authorities
  • Demonstrate respect toward school leaders

In Garoua (Week 1, Page 92), Amina learns about school authorities. The Headteacher and teachers guide our education and maintain school discipline.

lecons.titre: Personalities: Local Authorities
savoirs_faire: Name local authorities in the village and town (Traditional chief, quarterhead, mayor)
Describe roles of local authorities in keeping peace
Show respect for community leaders

exercices.enonce: Amina names local authorities in Garoua: Quarterhead, Chief, Mayor. Who heads a quarter?
exercices.astuce: The Quarterhead leads a neighborhood.

quiz.question: Who leads a traditional quarter in a town or village in Garoua?
quiz.explication: Quarterheads lead local quarters.

quiz.question: Who is the elected leader of a municipal council?
quiz.explication: The Mayor leads the municipal council.

quiz.question: Why are local authorities important in our community?
options: They maintain order, peace, and settle disputes
quiz.explication: Local leaders keep peace and resolve disputes.

lecons.contenu:
Personalities: Local Authorities

What you will learn:

  • Name local authorities in the village and town (Traditional chief, quarterhead, mayor)
  • Describe roles of local authorities in keeping peace
  • Show respect for community leaders

In Garoua (Week 2, Page 92), Amina explores local authorities. Traditional chiefs, quarterheads, and mayors preserve peace and manage local community development.

lecons.titre: Personalities: Political Figures
savoirs_faire: List national political figures and civic leaders
Explain how political leaders serve the country
Demonstrate patriotism and civic respect

exercices.enonce: Amina reads about political figures in Garoua. Who leads the nation?

quiz.question: Who represents citizens in the National Assembly?
quiz.explication: Parliamentarians represent citizens in assembly.

quiz.question: How do good citizens treat national political figures?
options: With civic respect and national pride
quiz.explication: Good citizens respect state institutions and leaders.

lecons.contenu:
Personalities: Political Figures

What you will learn:

  • List national political figures and civic leaders
  • Explain how political leaders serve the country
  • Demonstrate patriotism and civic respect

In Garoua (Week 3, Page 92), Amina learns about national political figures (the President, Ministers, Parliamentarians) who make laws and serve our nation.

lecons.titre: Personalities: Religious Authorities
savoirs_faire: Enumerate religious authorities (Pastors, imams, priests)
Explain the role of religious leaders in teaching moral values
Show tolerance and respect for all religious beliefs

exercices.enonce: Amina lists religious authorities in Garoua: Imam, Pastor, Priest. What do they teach?
exercices.astuce: Religious leaders teach peace, love, and respect.

quiz.question: Who leads prayers in a mosque in Garoua?
quiz.explication: An Imam leads prayers in a mosque.

quiz.question: Who leads worship in a church?
quiz.explication: Pastors and Priests lead church worship.

quiz.question: What essential value do religious leaders promote in Cameroon?
options: Love, moral values, and religious tolerance
quiz.explication: Religious leaders teach peace and moral values.

lecons.contenu:
Personalities: Religious Authorities

What you will learn:

  • Enumerate religious authorities (Pastors, imams, priests)
  • Explain the role of religious leaders in teaching moral values
  • Show tolerance and respect for all religious beliefs

In Garoua (Week 4, Page 92), Amina discovers religious authorities (Imams, Pastors, Priests). They guide spiritual life, teach moral values, and encourage peaceful religious coexistence!

lecons.titre: Components of a Computer System
savoirs_faire: Identify main components of a computer system (monitor, keyboard, mouse, system unit)
Draw basic computer components correctly
Handle computer parts gently

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla points to computer parts in Douala: Monitor, keyboard, mouse, system unit.
exercices.astuce: The monitor looks like a TV screen.

quiz.question: Which component of a computer displays images and text in Douala?
quiz.explication: The monitor displays visual information.

quiz.question: Which part is called the brain of the computer system?

quiz.question: What tool is used to type words into the computer?
quiz.explication: The keyboard is used for typing text.

lecons.contenu:
Components of a Computer System

What you will learn:

  • Identify main components of a computer system (monitor, keyboard, mouse, system unit)
  • Draw basic computer components correctly
  • Handle computer parts gently

In Douala (Week 1, Page 148), Ekwalla identifies main computer components: monitor (screen), keyboard, mouse, and system unit. We draw each part and learn their names!

lecons.titre: Uses of a Computer System
savoirs_faire: Identify and describe different uses of a computer
Explain how computers help in typing, drawing, and games
Demonstrate care when turning on a computer

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla uses a computer in Douala to draw pictures and type letters. Name one computer use.
exercices.astuce: Computers type text, draw pictures, and process data.

quiz.question: What activity can be done using a computer in Douala?
options: Typing stories, drawing pictures, and playing educational games
quiz.explication: Computers type, draw, calculate, and run programs.

quiz.question: Why are computers useful in schools and offices?
options: They store and process information quickly
quiz.explication: Computers process data with speed and accuracy.

quiz.question: What must we never pour on a computer keyboard?
quiz.explication: Liquids damage electronic computer circuits.

lecons.contenu:
Uses of a Computer System

What you will learn:

  • Identify and describe different uses of a computer
  • Explain how computers help in typing, drawing, and games
  • Demonstrate care when turning on a computer

In Douala (Week 2, Page 148), Ekwalla explores computer applications: typing documents, creating digital drawings, calculating numbers, and playing educational learning games!

lecons.titre: Uses of a Keyboard
savoirs_faire: State the correct use of a computer keyboard
Identify letter keys, number keys, and Spacebar
Practice pressing keys gently

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla presses the Spacebar in Douala to create spaces between words. What do letter keys do?
exercices.astuce: Letter keys type letters (A-Z).

quiz.question: Which long key on the keyboard creates a space between words?
quiz.explication: The Spacebar adds empty space between words.

quiz.question: What do number keys on a keyboard type?
quiz.explication: Number keys type digits 0 to 9.

quiz.question: How should keys on a keyboard be pressed?
quiz.explication: Gentle pressing protects keyboard springs.

lecons.contenu:
Uses of a Keyboard

What you will learn:

  • State the correct use of a computer keyboard
  • Identify letter keys, number keys, and Spacebar
  • Practice pressing keys gently

In Douala (Week 3, Page 148), Ekwalla learns the keyboard. We locate letter keys, number keys, and the long Spacebar, practicing gentle typing techniques!

lecons.titre: Uses of a Mouse
savoirs_faire: State the uses of a computer mouse
Demonstrate pointing, clicking, double-clicking, and dragging
Hold a mouse correctly on a mousepad

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla holds the mouse in Douala to move the arrow pointer on screen. Practice left click.
exercices.astuce: Left click selects items on screen.

quiz.question: What moves on the monitor screen when you slide the mouse in Douala?
quiz.explication: The mouse moves the screen arrow pointer.

quiz.question: What action selects an item on the screen?
quiz.explication: Clicking the left mouse button selects items.

quiz.question: Where should a mouse be placed for smooth movement?
quiz.explication: A mousepad ensures smooth mouse tracking.

lecons.contenu:
Uses of a Mouse

What you will learn:

  • State the uses of a computer mouse
  • Demonstrate pointing, clicking, double-clicking, and dragging
  • Hold a mouse correctly on a mousepad

In Douala (Week 4, Page 148), Ekwalla masters the mouse! We practice holding the mouse comfortably, moving the arrow pointer, clicking to select icons, and dragging items on screen.

lecons.titre: School Items, School Songs, Numbers 0-10, and Future Tense
savoirs_faire: Identify things found in the school and tell school stories
Read numbers from 0 to 10 in figures and words
Write future tense of verbs (will write, will sing)

exercices.astuce: Use 'will' to express the future tense.

quiz.question: Which of these is found in a classroom in Douala?

quiz.question: Read the number word: Z-E-R-O. What figure is it?
quiz.explication: Z-E-R-O is the figure 0.

quiz.question: Which verb is in the future tense?
quiz.explication: 'Will write' expresses future action.

lecons.contenu:
School Items, School Songs, Numbers 0-10, and Future Tense

What you will learn:

  • Identify things found in the school and tell school stories
  • Read numbers from 0 to 10 in figures and words
  • Write future tense of verbs (will write, will sing)

In Douala (Week 1, Page 10), Ayuk names school furniture, sings school welcome songs, reads numbers 0 to 10, and practices future tense verbs like 'I will write'.

lecons.titre: Classroom Items, Telling Time in Hours, and Common Adjectives
savoirs_faire: Identify and name things found in the classroom
Read numbers from 11 to 20 in words and figures and read time in hours
Use common adjectives to construct simple sentences

exercices.enonce: Ayuk tells the time in Douala: It is 8 o'clock. Use an adjective: Big desk.
exercices.astuce: Adjectives describe nouns (big, clean, new).

quiz.question: When the long hand points to 12 and the short hand to 8, what time is it?

quiz.question: Which word is an adjective describing a desk?
quiz.explication: 'Clean' is an adjective describing a noun.

quiz.question: Read the number in figures: 15. How is it written in words?
quiz.explication: 15 is written as Fifteen.

lecons.contenu:
Classroom Items, Telling Time in Hours, and Common Adjectives

What you will learn:

  • Identify and name things found in the classroom
  • Read numbers from 11 to 20 in words and figures and read time in hours
  • Use common adjectives to construct simple sentences

In Douala (Week 2, Page 11-12), Ayuk names classroom items, reads numbers 11 to 20, tells time in exact hours (8 o'clock), and describes objects using adjectives like 'clean desk'.

lecons.titre: School Role Plays, Upright Disjoint Script, and Adverbs of Place
savoirs_faire: Perform role-play sketches of different school characters
Write upright disjoint script for letters and words
Use adverbs of place (here, there, inside) in sentences

exercices.enonce: Ayuk role-plays a teacher in Douala: Sit here quietly. Use an adverb of place.
exercices.astuce: Adverbs of place tell where (here, there, inside).

quiz.question: Which word is an adverb of place showing location?
quiz.explication: 'Inside' tells where an action happens.

quiz.question: Who directs classroom activities in a school role play in Douala?

lecons.titre: National Emblems: The National Motto of Cameroon
savoirs_faire: State and explain the National Motto of Cameroon: 'Peace - Work - Fatherland'
Explain the meaning of Peace, Work, and Fatherland for every citizen
Apply the values of the national motto in school life

National Emblems: The National Motto of Cameroon

What you will learn:

In Bafoussam (Week 4, Page 97), Fotso recites and explains the National Motto ('Peace - Work - Fatherland' / 'Paix - Travail - Patrie') to finish March social studies with patriotic pride!

lecons.titre: Basic Notions of Abstraction: Differences in Environmental Objects
savoirs_faire: Explore basic notions of abstraction by identifying common objects in the environment
Distinguish differences in objects (cars, bicycles, trucks, houses)
Group objects by key characteristics (size, shape, function)

quiz.explication: Abstraction focuses on key shared features.

Basic Notions of Abstraction: Differences in Environmental Objects

What you will learn:

  • Distinguish differences in objects (cars, bicycles, trucks, houses)

lecons.titre: Computer Programs: Basic Tasks and Sorting Instructions

Demonstrate how computer programs sort out objects based on rules

Computer Programs: Basic Tasks and Sorting Instructions

In Douala (Week 2, Page 153), Kamdem learns how computer programs follow step-by-step instructions to sort out objects by shape, size, and category!

lecons.titre: Revision of Abstraction and Computer Programs
savoirs_faire: Revise basic notions of abstraction and computer program sorting tasks

Revision of Abstraction and Computer Programs

In Douala (Week 3, Page 154), Kamdem revises abstraction and computer sorting tasks, answering written questions in exercise books to complete Term 3 ICT with excellence!

lecons.titre: Traditional Communication Tools, Jumbled Words, and Demonstratives
savoirs_faire: Retell folktales and describe traditional tools of communication (talking drum, wooden gong, smoke signal)
Read short texts on traditional communication tools and build words with jumbled letters
Use demonstrative pronouns (this is, these are, that is, those are) to construct sentences

quiz.explication: Talking drums and wooden gongs passed traditional messages.

quiz.question: Which demonstrative phrase completes: '___ a traditional wooden gong' (singular near)?
quiz.explication: 'This is' refers to a single near object.

lecons.contenu:
Traditional Communication Tools, Jumbled Words, and Demonstratives

What you will learn:

  • Use demonstrative pronouns (this is, these are, that is, those are) to construct sentences

In Foumban (Week 1, Page 32-33), Tanyi describes traditional communication tools (talking drum, wooden gong), builds jumbled words, and uses demonstrative pronouns!

lecons.titre: Modern Communication Tools, 'er' Sound Words, and Upright Script
savoirs_faire: Describe modern tools of communication (telephone, radio, television, letter)

Write short upright words and use demonstratives (these are, those are)

quiz.question: Which modern communication device broadcasts news and audio programs in Foumban?

quiz.question: Which demonstrative phrase completes: '___ modern telephones on the table' (plural near)?
quiz.explication: 'These are' refers to plural nearby items.

lecons.contenu:
Modern Communication Tools, 'er' Sound Words, and Upright Script

What you will learn:

  • Describe modern tools of communication (telephone, radio, television, letter)
  • Read short texts on modern communication and read words with 'er' (farmer, driver, printer)
  • Write short upright words and use demonstratives (these are, those are)

In Foumban (Week 2, Page 33-34), Tanyi describes modern communication tools (radio, TV, telephone), reads 'er' sound words (farmer, driver), and practices upright script handwriting.

lecons.titre: Jolly Phonics Drum Song, 'dr' Sound Cluster Words, and Articles (a/an)
savoirs_faire: Sing Jolly Phonics drum song ('See me play upon my drum, d-d-d-d-d')
Read picture stories and read words containing the consonant cluster 'dr' (drum, dress, drink)
Write sentences on traditional communication and use articles 'a' and 'an'

exercices.enonce: Tanyi sings the drum song in Foumban: D-D-D-D drum! Use articles: A drum, an aeroplane.

quiz.question: Which consonant cluster is heard at the start of the word 'Drum'?

lecons.contenu:

What you will learn:

  • Read picture stories and read words containing the consonant cluster 'dr' (drum, dress, drink)
  • Write sentences on traditional communication and use articles 'a' and 'an'

In Foumban (Week 3, Page 35-36), Tanyi sings the Jolly Phonics drum song, reads 'dr' cluster words (drum, dress, drink), and uses articles 'a' and 'an' in sentences!

lecons.titre: Telephone Dialogue, Multi-Syllabic Words, and Modern Communication Importance

Write short sentences on the importance of modern communication tools

lecons.contenu:
Telephone Dialogue, Multi-Syllabic Words, and Modern Communication Importance

What you will learn:

  • Perform role-play sketches of telephone conversations and speak spontaneously
  • Read multi-syllabic words related to communication (tel-e-phone, ra-di-o, tel-e-vi-sion)
  • Write short sentences on the importance of modern communication tools

In Foumban (Week 4, Page 36-37), Tanyi performs phone conversation sketches, reads multi-syllabic words (tel-e-phone, ra-di-o), and writes about communication importance to finish Class 1 English!

lecons.titre: Introduction to Fractions (Half ½), Money Comparison (<, >), and Graph Data
savoirs_faire: Introduce and identify the fraction one half (½) by dividing shapes/objects into 2 equal parts
Compare money values using comparison symbols (< and >)
Represent simple data using basic pictographs and charts

quiz.explication: 1 out of 2 equal parts is ½.

quiz.question: How many halves make one whole object?
quiz.explication: Two halves make one whole.

lecons.contenu:
Introduction to Fractions (Half ½), Money Comparison (<, >), and Graph Data

What you will learn:

  • Introduce and identify the fraction one half (½) by dividing shapes/objects into 2 equal parts
  • Compare money values using comparison symbols (< and >)
  • Represent simple data using basic pictographs and charts

In Buea (Week 1, Page 59), Ekema discovers fractions (half ½), compares money values using < and > (100 FCFA > 50 FCFA), and represents data on simple pictographs!

lecons.titre: Fractions ½ (Shading Half), Money Comparison, and Number Ranking

Compare money amounts using symbols < and >
Arrange numbers in ascending (smallest to largest) and descending order

quiz.explication: 10, 25, 40 goes from smallest to largest.

quiz.question: If a rectangle is divided into 2 equal halves, how many parts do you shade to show ½?
quiz.explication: Shading 1 part out of 2 shows ½.

quiz.question: Compare money values: 25 FCFA ___ 75 FCFA.
quiz.explication: 25 FCFA is less than 75 FCFA -> 25 < 75.

lecons.contenu:
Fractions ½ (Shading Half), Money Comparison, and Number Ranking

What you will learn:

  • Identify and shade the fraction one half (½) on circles, squares, and rectangles
  • Compare money amounts using symbols < and >
  • Arrange numbers in ascending (smallest to largest) and descending order

In Buea (Week 2, Page 60), Ekema shades ½ of geometric shapes, compares money amounts using < and >, and ranks numbers in ascending and descending order!

lecons.titre: Fractions ¼ and ¾ (Shading Quarters), Money Comparison, and Tallying

Compare money values using < and >
Tally numbers and data in groups of 5 using tally marks (||||)

lecons.contenu:
Fractions ¼ and ¾ (Shading Quarters), Money Comparison, and Tallying

What you will learn:

  • Identify and shade the fractions one quarter (¼) and three quarters (¾)
  • Compare money values using < and >
  • Tally numbers and data in groups of 5 using tally marks (||||)

In Buea (Week 3, Page 60-61), Ekema discovers quarters (¼ and ¾), shades fractional parts, compares money values, and tallies data in bundles of 5!

lecons.titre: Fraction Shading (½, ¼, ¾), Money Revision, and Bar Graph Representation

lecons.contenu:
Fraction Shading (½, ¼, ¾), Money Revision, and Bar Graph Representation

What you will learn:

  • Identify and shade mixed fractions (½, ¼, ¾) on various shapes
  • Revise money comparison and ranking up to 200 FCFA
  • Represent simple survey data using bar graphs and tallies

In Buea (Week 4, Page 61), Ekema shades fractions (½, ¼, ¾), revises money comparisons, and builds simple bar graphs to complete Class 1 mathematics with total mastery!

lecons.titre: Good Health Habits and Communication Tools Materials

Practicing Health Habits and Sound Production in Instruments

lecons.titre: Pollution and Waste Management and Electronic Tools Materials

Pollution and Waste Management and Electronic Tools Materials

lecons.titre: Actions quotidiennes (Qu'est-ce que tu fais ?) et homophones leur / leurs

Actions quotidiennes (Qu'est-ce que tu fais ?) et homophones leur / leurs
